meaning: A service that queues jobs and starts instances for them, such as AWS Batch or AWS PCS. It is also called a scheduler.
The way you pay for an instance, together with what AWS promises in return. The options are On-Demand, Spot Instances, Savings Plans, Capacity Blocks for ML and On-Demand Capacity Reservations.

A group of jobs with the same duration, coupling and interruptibility. Section 20 names five: Independent tasks, Long single-machine runs, Multi-node training, Always-on streams and Real-time on the robot.
AWS's own Arm CPUs. Graviton instances, such as C8g and M8g, have no GPU.
The EC2 GPU instance families whose GPUs have RT cores. They are used for rendering and for jobs that need one GPU.
The EC2 instance families with the data-centre GPUs used for training. These GPUs have no RT cores.
The hardware units in a GPU that an RTX renderer requires.
The EC2 network device that lets many nodes train together as one job.
A managed service that runs one training container and keeps nothing running after it finishes.
A managed job queue that starts instances for jobs and holds no instances while the queue is empty.
A single AWS Batch submission that fans out into as many as 10,000 child jobs.
A persistent cluster in which AWS replaces faulty hardware. You schedule jobs on it with Slurm or Kubernetes.
A managed Slurm service. AWS runs the Slurm controller, and the compute node groups start instances for waiting jobs and can scale back to zero.
The AWS PCS object that says which instances to launch, how many, and with which purchase option. Each group has one purchase option.
The job scheduler of classic supercomputing. You submit jobs to it with commands such as sbatch.
Kubernetes with the control plane run by AWS.
A mode of EKS in which AWS also runs the nodes.
A machine outside AWS, such as a lab workstation, that joins an EKS cluster as one of its nodes.
An instance you pay for while you use it, with no commitment. AWS does not promise that an instance is free when you ask for one.
Spare EC2 capacity that AWS can reclaim. AWS sends a two-minute warning on a best-effort basis, and the warning can be missing.
A prepaid reservation of GPU instances with a fixed start and end date.
The same kind of reservation as a Capacity Block, made through SageMaker.
A discount on the bill for the instances you run.
Capacity held for one named instance type in one Availability Zone. You pay the On-Demand rate for it whether or not an instance runs in it.
AWS's own training chip.
A rack-scale EC2 system at the top of the P range.
The AWS service that sends software components to devices, such as the robot's onboard computer.
The AWS managed render farm.
The unit in which EC2 counts processor capacity.
